title: Optimizing Large TypeScript Projects knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the strongest evidence that an application design is ready for review?
options: Only a screenshot of the happy path.
A successful compile with no runtime checks or acceptance criteria.
Clear domain contracts, implemented behavior, tests for normal and failure cases, and reproducible setup/documentation.
A large number of abstractions without tests.
questions.answer_key: Clear domain contracts, implemented behavior, tests for normal and failure cases, and reproducible setup/documentation.
questions.explanation: Production-oriented work is supported by explicit acceptance criteria and repeatable evidence.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Optimizing Large TypeScript Projects”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with reducing unnecessary type complexity and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with reducing unnecessary type complexity and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Reducing unnecessary type complexity”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Optimizing Large TypeScript Projects”?
options: Check project references and build boundaries, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume diagnosing expensive compiler workloads is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check project references and build boundaries, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Project references and build boundaries”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
